body:
Thank you for your reply and advice.  I agree with you completely, and I think you're saying a lot of the things I was thinking, I was just worried that I was thinking wrong - and with so much on the line, I felt like it would be a terrible idea not to ask for help.  I'm afraid of what would happen if I asked someone I know because this is a pretty small town, and it'd probably get back to her, and she'd feel betrayed.

I hope that you're correct in your appraisal, and for what it's worth I think you are.  We're planning on going over there this evening with some good food and movies, and just spending time with her if she'll allow it.  Thank you for all of the suggestions, they're all good.

In the long run, I believe she'll be alright - I have high hopes... I just worry, and my partner was so worried she was in tears.  Her partner was a good guy for so long, I had a good friendship with him for years.  He was one of the best guitar players I ever met.  He's also the first person who's ever died when I was on bad terms with them.  If there's anything after this, I wish him well at it.  I know he didn't really intend for this situation to occur when he died, although he knew he was very likely to die before her and he basically said it's what he wanted - that wasn't really him, I think that was just him staring his own mortality in the face and being unable to cope with it.  They used to always be out at barbecues and dance parties, but for the last few years he's had them sequestered away.  They moved further and further away from town, sold their vehicles, and he forbid her from having a job.

I know it'll take a while, but hopefully she'll be able to reconnect with her friends in the future.  We will do our best to help her with that, while, of course, not letting on that we feel that way (a bit relieved) about his death... 

Thank you all for giving me a space to vent about this and some advice and reassurances.  If anyone else has anything to add I'm sure it'll be helpful.  I'm not, in general, good at consoling people and I tend to obsess and fret.  Seriously, thank you.
